mainTopic: Latecomers and קדושה, interrupting the עמידה, and רבי יהודה's view on a בעל קרי
overview: The גמרא finishes explaining why two rulings about not repeating תפילה are both needed. Then רב הונא and רבי יהושע בן לוי argue about a latecomer to shul. He may start his עמידה only if he can finish before the שליח צבור reaches מודים, or, according to רבי יהושע בן לוי, קדושה. The argument depends on whether a יחיד may say קדושה, and a גזירה שוה of 'תוך' shows that any דבר שבקדושה needs ten. Everyone agrees one does not interrupt the עמידה for קדושה, and the הלכה is that one does not interrupt even for יהא שמו הגדול מבורך. The גמרא then challenges רבי יהודה of our משנה, who lets a בעל קרי say ברכות, from the פסוקים about הר סיני. It answers that those סמוכים are needed for another teaching, after proving where רבי יהודה does and does not learn from סמוכים. Finally, a משנה about טבילה for קרי is used to show that רבי יהודה seems to require טבילה for a plain בעל קרי, and this discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why the synagogue ruling is needed
steps.stepSummary: Without the second ruling, we might think that someone who davened alone and then meets a צבור counts as if he never davened. So that ruling is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: [If we only had the first ruling, we would say it applies when someone davened alone and repeats alone,] or davened with a צבור and repeats with a צבור. But a יחיד compared to a צבור is treated like someone who has not davened. So the second ruling teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is in the middle of a צריכא, explaining why we need both of two earlier rulings about someone who already davened. This first half shows why the ruling about walking into a shul is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we only had the first ruling (he remembers mid-תפילה that he already davened, so he stops), we might limit it to repeating in the same setting. We might think davening alone does not count once a צבור is present. The second ruling teaches that even then, he does not just repeat.

keyTerms.meaning: a congregation, a group davening together
an individual davening by himself
in relation to, compared to
it teaches us (the new point)

phrases.english: or a congregation and a congregation;
phrases.notes: He davened with a צבור and then started again with a צבור.

phrases.english: but an individual compared to a congregation

steps.title: Why the stopping ruling is needed, so both are needed
steps.stepSummary: Without the first ruling, we might think he may keep going once he has already started. So both rulings are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it had only taught us here [the shul case], I would say that is because he had not started yet. But there, where he already started, I would say no [he may continue]. So both are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the צריכא by showing why the first ruling is also needed, then concludes that both rulings are necessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The shul case is about someone who has not started yet, and it is easy to tell him not to begin. Without the first ruling, we might say that someone already in the middle may finish. The first ruling teaches that even mid-תפילה he stops.

keyTerms.meaning: it had taught us
he began
I would say no (the rule would not apply)
it is necessary (both statements are needed)

steps.whatToRemember: Both rulings are needed. One covers someone already in the middle, and the other covers a יחיד meeting a צבור.

phrases.english: And if it had taught us only here,
phrases.notes: "Here" is the case of walking into the shul and finding the צבור davening.

phrases.english: [I would say it is] because he did not begin it,
but there, where he already began it,
I would say no.
It is necessary [to have both].

steps.title: רב הונא: finish before מודים
steps.stepSummary: A latecomer may start his עמידה only if he can finish before the שליח צבור reaches מודים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: Someone who walks into shul and finds the צבור davening may daven if he can start and finish before the שליח צבור reaches מודים. If not, he should not daven [now].
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רב הונא rules on when a latecomer may start his own עמידה while the צבור is davening.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The test is timing. He starts only if he will be done before the שליח צבור gets to מודים. If he cannot make it, he should wait.

keyTerms.meaning: synagogue
the prayer leader, who repeats the עמידה aloud
the blessing of thanks in the עמידה
he should pray

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
One who enters a synagogue

if he can begin and finish

steps.title: רבי יהושע בן לוי: finish before קדושה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי sets an earlier deadline: he must finish before קדושה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: If he can start and finish before the שליח צבור reaches קדושה, he may daven. If not, he should not daven.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא gives a different deadline for the same case, so now there is a מחלוקת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case and the structure are the same as רב הונא's. Only the deadline changes, from מודים to קדושה, which comes earlier in the חזרת הש״ץ. That makes his rule stricter.

keyTerms.meaning: the sanctification said responsively in the חזרת הש״ץ
to start and to finish

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
If he can begin and finish

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁלֹּא יַגִּיעַ שְׁלִיחַ צִבּוּר לִ״קְדוּשָּׁה״ —
phrases.english: before the prayer leader reaches "Kedusha" —
he should pray,
and if not — he should not pray.

steps.triggerLanguage: רבי יהושע בן לוי אמר: אם יכול להתחיל ולגמור
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב הונא on the deadline
steps.mimraCoreRuling: He may start only if he can finish before the שליח צבור reaches קדושה.

steps.title: What is the argument about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what idea underlies the two deadlines.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It asks for the reason behind the מחלוקת, and the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree he must finish by some point. The גמרא wants to know what principle makes one say מודים and the other say קדושה.

keyTerms.meaning: about what do they disagree?

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.triggerLanguage: במאי קא מפלגי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the dispute in steps 3-4
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying principle behind מודים versus קדושה

steps.title: Can a יחיד say קדושה?
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא holds a יחיד may say קדושה alone; רבי יהושע בן לוי holds he may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: One master holds a יחיד says קדושה, and the other master holds a יחיד does not say קדושה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. The argument depends on whether a person davening alone may say קדושה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב הונא, a יחיד can say קדושה himself, so he does not need to be done in time for the צבור's קדושה. For רבי יהושע בן לוי, a יחיד cannot say קדושה, so he must finish in time to say it with the צבור.

keyTerms.meaning: one master holds
and the other master holds

steps.confusionAlert: The first "מר" here is רב הונא (a יחיד may say קדושה), and the second is רבי יהושע בן לוי (he may not). Don't mix them up.

phrases.english: One master holds an individual says "Kedusha,"
phrases.notes: This is רב הונא.

phrases.english: and the other master holds an individual does not say "Kedusha."
phrases.notes: This is רבי יהושע בן לוי.

steps.triggerLanguage: מר סבר יחיד אומר קדושה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 5
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The dispute is whether a יחיד may say קדושה alone

steps.title: A פסוק shows קדושה needs ten
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה derives from a פסוק that any דבר שבקדושה needs at least ten, supporting רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so said רב אדא בר אהבה: How do we know that a יחיד does not say קדושה? Because it says, "And I shall be sanctified among the children of Israel." Any matter of holiness needs no fewer than ten.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for the view that a יחיד may not say קדושה. It quotes רב אדא בר אהבה, who learns it from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says ה׳ is sanctified "among" בני ישראל, which means in a group. From this comes a general rule: any דבר שבקדושה needs at least ten people. This backs רבי יהושע בן לוי's position.

keyTerms.meaning: from where do we know?
and I shall be sanctified
a matter of holiness (like קדושה)
ten (a מנין)

steps.whatToRemember: A יחיד does not say קדושה, because any דבר שבקדושה needs at least ten. This supports רבי יהושע בן לוי, whose deadline is קדושה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the well-known rule that a דבר שבקדושה requires a מנין of ten.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה:
phrases.english: And so said Rav Adda bar Ahava:
From where do we know that an individual does not say "Kedusha"?
As it says: "And I shall be sanctified among the children of Israel,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:32

phrases.english: any matter of holiness
may not be with fewer than ten.

steps.triggerLanguage: וכן אמר רב אדא בר אהבה: מנין שאין היחיד אומר קדושה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the second view in step 6
steps.raayaObject: That a יחיד does not say קדושה (רבי יהושע בן לוי's view)
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 22:32, "ונקדשתי בתוך בני ישראל," as explained by רב אדא בר אהבה

steps.title: How does the verse show that ten are needed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the פסוק quoted by רב אדא בר אהבה teaches that a דבר שבקדושה needs ten.
steps.simpleTranslation: How is this learned from that verse?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question about the proof in Step 7. This sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'I will be made holy among בני ישראל', but it never mentions the number ten. So the גמרא wants to know where the number ten comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: How is it implied? Where do we see it?

phrases.english: How is this implied?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the proof-verse in Step 7 actually works.
steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי מַשְׁמַע
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the פסוק 'ונקדשתי בתוך בני ישראל' implies a minimum of ten.

steps.title: The word 'among' links to the congregation of קרח
steps.stepSummary: רבנאי teaches a גזירה שוה between the two uses of the word תוך. Just as 'among' in the story of קרח means ten, 'among' in ונקדשתי also means ten.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבנאי, the brother of רבי חייא בר אבא, taught: it is learned from 'among' and 'among'. Here it says 'I will be made holy among בני ישראל', and there it says 'Separate yourselves from among this congregation'. Just as there it means ten, so too here it means ten.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by linking the same word, תוך ('among'), in two different פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This tool is called a גזירה שוה: the same word in two places teaches that both places share the same law. In the story of קרח, תוך refers to an עדה, a group of at least ten. So תוך in ונקדשתי also means a group of ten.

keyTerms.meaning: Learning a law from the same word appearing in two פסוקים
It comes (it is learned from)
Among, in the midst of
Just as there, so too here

phrases.aramaic: דְּתָנֵי רַבְנַאי אֲחוּהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא:
phrases.english: As רבנאי, the brother of רבי חייא בר אבא, taught:
It is learned from 'among' and 'among'.
phrases.notes: The same word appears in two פסוקים, so we learn one from the other.

phrases.english: It is written here: 'And I will be made holy among בני ישראל',
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:32

phrases.english: and it is written there: 'Separate yourselves from among this congregation',
phrases.notes: במדבר 16:21, said about the group of קרח.

phrases.english: Just as there, it means ten,
so too here, it means ten.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 8 by explaining how the verse yields the number ten.
steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתָנֵי רַבְנַאי אֲחוּהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה of תוך/תוך links ונקדשתי to the עדה of קרח, which is ten.

steps.title: Everyone agrees you do not stop your עמידה for קדושה
steps.stepSummary: Both רב הונא and רבי יהושע בן לוי agree that a person in the middle of his עמידה does not stop to answer קדושה.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, everyone agrees that he does not interrupt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a point that both sides agree on. A person who is in the middle of the עמידה does not stop to answer קדושה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא and רבי יהושע בן לוי argued about whether one person alone may say קדושה. But neither one says you may interrupt the עמידה for it. That is why the latecomer must finish his עמידה before the שליח צבור reaches that point.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees
In any case, at least
He certainly does not interrupt

phrases.english: And in any case, according to everyone,
phrases.notes: 'Everyone' means both רב הונא and רבי יהושע בן לוי.

phrases.english: he does not interrupt.
phrases.notes: He doesn't stop his עמידה to answer קדושה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the debate with a point of agreement between both opinions.
steps.triggerLanguage: וּדְכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא מִיהַת מִפְסָק לָא פָּסֵיק
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: No one may interrupt the עמידה to answer קדושה; that is the reason behind the time limits.
steps.whatToRemember: Both opinions agree that you never stop in the middle of the עמידה for קדושה. They only argue about the deadline for finishing.

steps.title: May one stop the עמידה to answer יהא שמו הגדול מבורך?
steps.stepSummary: The study hall asks whether a person may interrupt his עמידה to answer יהא שמו הגדול מבורך in קדיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: may one interrupt in order to say 'May His great name be blessed'?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we know you do not stop for קדושה, the גמרא asks a new question about the response in קדיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a real open question, not a challenge. The idea is that יהא שמו הגדול מבורך might be important enough to be an exception, even though קדושה is not.

keyTerms.meaning: They asked (a question raised in the study hall)
To interrupt
'May His great name be blessed', the main response in קדיש

phrases.english: They asked:
What is the law about interrupting,
in order to say 'May His great name be blessed'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from קדושה to a related case, the response in קדיש.
steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: מַהוּ לְהַפְסִיק
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether יהא שמו הגדול מבורך justifies interrupting the עמידה.

steps.title: רב דימי reports: stop for nothing except יהא שמו הגדול מבורך
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי quotes students of רבי יוחנן: one does not interrupt for anything except יהא שמו הגדול מבורך. Even someone studying מעשה מרכבה stops for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came, he said: רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון, students of רבי יוחנן, say: one does not interrupt for anything except 'May His great name be blessed'. Even someone busy with מעשה מרכבה stops for it.
steps.whatsHappening: An answer arrives from ארץ ישראל: יהא שמו הגדול מבורך is so important that you may stop even the עמידה for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To show how important this response is, they point to מעשה מרכבה, the holiest kind of learning. If you stop even that, then this response is above almost everything else.

keyTerms.meaning: When he came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)
The deep, holy study of the Divine Chariot (יחזקאל chapter 1)
He stops

phrases.english: When רב דימי came, he said:
רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון,
students of רבי יוחנן, say:
For everything, we do not interrupt,
except for 'May His great name be blessed'.
For even one busy with מעשה מרכבה stops.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 11.
steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי, אָמַר
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: One may interrupt for יהא שמו הגדול מבורך, and for nothing else.

steps.title: The הלכה does not follow this view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules that the הלכה is not like the view רב דימי reported.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is not like him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes this question with a ruling: in practice, you do not stop the עמידה even for יהא שמו הגדול מבורך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea that יהא שמו הגדול מבורך is very important still stands. But the practical rule is that the עמידה is not interrupted, just like with קדושה.

keyTerms.meaning: The הלכה is not like him

phrases.english: And the הלכה is not in accordance with him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the practical ruling that rejects Step 12.
steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֵית הִלְכְתָא כְּוָתֵיהּ
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In practice, one does not interrupt the עמידה even for יהא שמו הגדול מבורך.
steps.whatToRemember: The bottom line: the עמידה is not interrupted, not for קדושה and not for יהא שמו הגדול מבורך.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: רבי יהודה says a בעל קרי makes the ברכות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יהודה's ruling from the משנה that a בעל קרי says the ברכות before and after.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: he says the blessing before them and after them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a line in the משנה about a בעל קרי. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא in the משנה limited what a בעל קרי may say. רבי יהודה says he recites all the ברכות, both before and after. This quote is the base text for the challenge that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: A man who had a seminal emission and has not yet immersed
Says the blessings before and after them

phrases.english: רבי יהודה says:
phrases.notes: We're back in our משנה now, in the case of a בעל קרי.

phrases.english: He says the blessing before them and after them.
phrases.notes: 'Them' means קריאת שמע and food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic by quoting the משנה.
steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מְבָרֵךְ לִפְנֵיהֶם וּלְאַחֲרֵיהֶם
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, a בעל קרי recites the blessings before and after שמע and food.

steps.title: Challenge: a בעל קרי is forbidden in Torah learning
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי יהודה really allows a בעל קרי to say words of Torah. רבי יהושע בן לוי learns from the פסוקים about הר סיני that a בעל קרי is forbidden to learn Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean רבי יהודה holds that a בעל קרי is allowed to say words of Torah? But רבי יהושע בן לוי said: from where do we know that a בעל קרי is forbidden to learn Torah? As it says, 'Make them known to your children and your children's children', and right next to it, 'The day that you stood…'. Just as there, those who were בעלי קרי were forbidden, so too here, those who are בעלי קרי are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יהודה. If he lets a בעל קרי say ברכות, he seems to allow Torah words. But a פסוק shows that a בעל קרי is forbidden to learn Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע בן לוי uses סמוכים, two פסוקים placed next to each other. The מצוה to teach Torah to your children sits right next to the day at הר סיני. At סיני a בעל קרי could not take part, so Torah learning in every generation has the same rule. That seems to clash with רבי יהודה's lenient ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Does this mean to say…? (opens a challenge)
But didn't (so-and-so) say…!
Words of Torah, Torah learning
Next to it (a פסוק placed right beside another)

phrases.english: Does this mean that רבי יהודה holds
that a בעל קרי is allowed to say words of Torah?
But didn't רבי יהושע בן לוי say:
From where do we know that a בעל קרי
is forbidden to say words of Torah?
As it says: 'And you shall make them known to your children and your children's children',
phrases.notes: דברים 4:9

phrases.english: and right next to it: 'The day that you stood, etc.'
phrases.notes: דברים 4:10. This is about the day the Jews stood at הר סיני.

phrases.english: Just as there, those who were בעלי קרי were forbidden,
phrases.notes: 'There' means at הר סיני, when the people had to stay pure.

phrases.english: so too here, those who are בעלי קרי are forbidden!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling of רבי יהודה quoted in Step 14.
steps.triggerLanguage: לְמֵימְרָא דְקָסָבַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בַּעַל קֶרִי מוּתָּר בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's ruling that a בעל קרי recites ברכות before and after.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Saying ברכות means a בעל קרי would be allowed words of Torah. But רבי יהושע בן לוי derives from the סמוכים to הר סיני that a בעל קרי is forbidden in Torah learning.
steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether ברכות count as prayer. The גמרא assumes that letting a בעל קרי say these ברכות means he is allowed to say holy Torah words, and that is what clashes with רבי יהושע בן לוי.

steps.title: Blocking the escape: רבי יהודה learns from סמוכים in משנה תורה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא blocks a possible answer: one might say רבי יהודה does not learn from סמוכים. But רב יוסף taught that רבי יהודה does learn from סמוכים in משנה תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say that רבי יהודה does not learn from verses placed next to each other, didn't רב יוסף say: even someone who does not learn from סמוכים in the whole Torah does learn from them in משנה תורה. For רבי יהודה does not learn from סמוכים in the whole Torah, yet in משנה תורה he does.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא expects that someone will try to defend רבי יהודה by saying he doesn't learn from verses placed side by side. It shuts that defense down by quoting רב יוסף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע בן לוי's proof in Step 15 that a בעל קרי may not learn Torah comes from two verses placed next to each other. If רבי יהודה ignored סמוכים, he could reject that proof. But רב יוסף says רבי יהודה does use סמוכים in ספר דברים, and those verses are in דברים, so the question against רבי יהודה stays strong.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (the גמרא predicts an answer before it is given)
He learns a law from (expounds) a verse
Verses placed right next to each other, read as teaching something together
The fifth book of the Torah, ספר דברים
But didn't he say? (introduces a challenge)

steps.confusionAlert: Step 16 is not taking רבי יהודה's side. The גמרא raises a possible defense for him only to knock it down, so the question against him gets stronger.

phrases.english: And if you will say that Rabbi Yehuda
does not expound "juxtaposed verses,"
phrases.notes: The proof in Step 15 came from two verses placed next to each other, so this would be a way out for רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: but didn't Rav Yosef say:
Even one who does not expound juxtaposed verses
throughout the Torah,
in Mishne Torah, does expound them.
phrases.notes: משנה תורה is the book of דברים, where the פסוקים about הר סיני from Step 15 are.

phrases.english: For Rabbi Yehuda does not expound juxtaposed verses
throughout the entire Torah
and in Mishne Torah he does expound them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה לָא דָּרֵישׁ סְמוּכִים, וְהָאָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens the קשיא of Step 15 by closing a possible defense of רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaTarget: A possible defense of רבי יהודה: that he does not learn from סמוכים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב יוסף says רבי יהודה does learn from סמוכים in משנה תורה, and the proof verses are in משנה תורה.

steps.title: Where do we see רבי יהודה ignore סמוכים in the rest of the Torah?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a source that רבי יהודה does not learn from סמוכים elsewhere in the Torah. It begins a ברייתא in which בן עזאי learns stoning for a מכשפה from סמוכים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And in the whole Torah, how do we know he doesn't learn from סמוכים? As it was taught: בן עזאי says: it says 'A sorceress you shall not let live,' and it says 'Whoever lies with an animal shall surely be put to death.' The Torah placed them next to each other to teach: just as one who lies with an animal is stoned, so too a sorceress is stoned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now proves the first half of רב יוסף's rule. It quotes בן עזאי's opinion, which sets up רבי יהודה's reply in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בן עזאי uses a סמוכים argument: two verses side by side share the same punishment, which is stoning. This is the view רבי יהודה is about to argue against. That reply will show that he does not accept סמוכים outside of דברים.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this?
A sorceress
Stoning, one of the four death penalties of בית דין
The Torah placed this topic next to that one

phrases.english: And throughout the entire Torah,
from where do we know that he does not expound them?
As it was taught in a baraita: Ben Azzai says:
It is said: "A sorceress you shall not let live,"
phrases.notes: שמות 22:17

phrases.aramaic: וְנֶאֱמַר ״כׇּל שׁוֹכֵב עִם בְּהֵמָה מוֹת יוּמָת״
phrases.english: and it is said: "Whoever lies with an animal shall surely be put to death"
phrases.notes: שמות 22:18, the very next פסוק.

phrases.english: The Torah placed this matter next to that one, to say:
just as one who lies with an animal is put to death by stoning,
so too a sorceress is also put to death by stoning.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבְכׇל הַתּוֹרָה כּוּלָּהּ מְנָא לַן דְּלָא דָּרֵישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the first half of רב יוסף's statement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Proof that רבי יהודה does not learn from סמוכים outside משנה תורה.

steps.title: רבי יהודה rejects learning stoning from סמוכים
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה refuses to sentence someone to stoning just because two verses are next to each other. He learns the stoning of a מכשפה from אוב and ידעוני instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said to him: Just because the Torah placed it next to that verse, should we take this person out to be stoned? Rather, אוב and ידעוני were included among all sorcerers. Why were they singled out? To compare to them and tell you: just as אוב and ידעוני are stoned, so too a sorceress is stoned.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה argues with בן עזאי. He does not accept a סמוכים proof, and he gets the same law from a different source. This proves the first half of רב יוסף's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree that a מכשפה is stoned, but they disagree about the method. רבי יהודה won't rely on verses being next to each other, so he uses a different method. אוב and ידעוני are types of sorcery that the Torah singled out for stoning, and that teaches about every sorceress. This clearly shows רבי יהודה does not learn from סמוכים in the rest of the Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: A medium, a type of sorcerer who calls up the dead
A wizard, another type of sorcerer
Included in a larger group
To compare and learn one case from another

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה does not learn laws from verses placed side by side in most of the Torah. The case of the מכשפה proves this: he gets her stoning from אוב and ידעוני, not from the next verse.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said to him:
And just because the Torah placed this matter next to that one,
shall we take this person out to be stoned?
Rather: a medium and a wizard
were included among all sorcerers,
and why were they singled out?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 20:27, where the Torah says they are stoned.

phrases.english: To compare to them and to tell you:
just as a medium and a wizard are put to death by stoning,
so too a sorceress is put to death by stoning.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: וְכִי מִפְּנֵי שֶׁסְּמָכוֹ עִנְיָן לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer to Step 17's question by showing רבי יהודה rejecting בן עזאי's סמוכים proof.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהודה does not learn from סמוכים in the Torah outside משנה תורה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא in which רבי יהודה rejects בן עזאי's סמוכים proof for stoning a מכשפה.

steps.title: Where do we see רבי יהודה use סמוכים in משנה תורה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a source that רבי יהודה does learn from סמוכים in משנה תורה. It begins a ברייתא of רבי אליעזר about marrying a woman violated or seduced by one's father or son.
steps.simpleTranslation: And in משנה תורה, how do we know he does learn from סמוכים? As it was taught: רבי אליעזר says: a man may marry a woman raped by his father or seduced by his father, a woman raped by his son or seduced by his son.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to the second half of רב יוסף's rule. It starts quoting a ברייתא. The part that connects it to רבי יהודה comes next, so this step is setting up that proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר's ruling says the ban on a father's or son's wife does not apply to a woman he raped or seduced. The גמרא is laying out this ruling first. The following lines will show how רבי יהודה disagrees by using verses that sit next to each other in דברים.

keyTerms.meaning: Marries
A woman who was raped by
A woman who was seduced by

phrases.english: And in Mishne Torah, from where do we know that he expounds them?
As it was taught in a baraita: Rabbi Eliezer says:
A man may marry a woman raped by his father
and a woman seduced by his father,
a woman raped by his son and a woman seduced by his son.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבְמִשְׁנֵה תוֹרָה מְנָא לַן דְּדָרֵישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the first half of רב יוסף's rule to its second half.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Proof that רבי יהודה does learn from סמוכים in משנה תורה.

steps.title: רבי יהודה forbids marrying a woman his father raped or seduced
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends with רבי יהודה's ruling. רב explains that it comes from the end of the פסוק 'ולא יגלה כנף אביו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה forbids a man to marry a woman his father raped or seduced. רב גידל said in the name of רב: What is רבי יהודה's reason? It is written: 'A man shall not take his father's wife, and shall not uncover his father's skirt.' This teaches that a 'skirt' his father has seen, he may not uncover.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the ברייתא it started in the last step. רבי יהודה forbids a son to marry a woman his father raped or seduced, and רב gives the source from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'His father's wife' would only cover a woman his father married. The extra words 'his father's skirt' include any woman his father was with, even without marriage. This sets up the next step, which shows that the פסוק is read this way only because of the verses next to it.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman his father forced
A woman his father seduced
His father's skirt; here it means a woman his father was intimate with
What is the reason?

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda forbids
a woman raped by his father and a woman seduced by his father.
phrases.notes: He means the son may not marry her.

phrases.english: And Rav Giddel said in the name of Rav:
What is Rabbi Yehuda's reason?

phrases.aramaic: — דִּכְתִיב: ״לֹא יִקַּח אִישׁ אֶת אֵשֶׁת אָבִיו
phrases.english: As it is written: 'A man shall not take his father's wife,'
phrases.notes: דברים 23:1

phrases.english: 'and shall not uncover his father's skirt.'
A 'skirt' that his father has seen, he may not uncover.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא that step 19 began. It gives רבי יהודה's ruling and רב's source for it.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה learns from סמוכים in משנה תורה (finished in the next step)
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי אליעזר and רב's explanation of רבי יהודה's opinion

steps.title: The verse is about rape because of the verse next to it
steps.stepSummary: We know the פסוק is talking about a woman the father raped because the verses right before it discuss rape. This is a use of סמוכים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do we know the verse is talking about a woman raped by his father? Because right next to it is written: 'And the man who lay with her shall give...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows exactly where רבי יהודה uses סמוכים. He reads the 'father's skirt' פסוק as being about rape only because it sits right after the section about rape.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This completes the proof that רב יוסף's claim was true: in משנה תורה, רבי יהודה does learn from verses placed side by side. That brings back the original question: why doesn't he learn the בעל קרי ban from סמוכים?

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do we know?
Because it is placed right next to it

steps.confusionAlert: רב's reason in step 20 came from the words of the פסוק. The rape part is still learned from סמוכים, and that is the point the גמרא needs.

phrases.english: And from where do we know that it is written about a woman raped by his father?
Because next to it is written:
'And the man who lay with her shall give, etc.'
phrases.notes: דברים 22:29

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִמַּאי דְּבַאֲנוּסַת אָבִיו כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the reading in step 20 depends on סמוכים. This proves רב יוסף's claim from step 16.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהודה learns from סמוכים in משנה תורה
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברים 22:29 placed right next to דברים 23:1

steps.title: Those verses are needed for a different teaching
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה does learn from סמוכים in משנה תורה. But the verses about הר חורב are already used for רבי יהושע בן לוי's teaching about teaching one's son Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: They answered: Yes, in משנה תורה he does learn from verses next to each other. But he needs these particular verses for another teaching of רבי יהושע בן לוי. רבי יהושע בן לוי said: Whoever teaches his son Torah, the verse treats him as if he received it at הר חורב. As it says, 'And you shall make them known to your children and your children's children,' and right after it is written, 'The day that you stood before ה׳ your God at חורב.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 15. רבי יהודה does use סמוכים in משנה תורה, but these specific verses are already being used to teach something else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer does not deny that רבי יהודה learns from סמוכים. It explains that one pair of side-by-side verses teaches one lesson. These verses are used to praise a father who teaches his son Torah, so they cannot also forbid a בעל קרי from learning.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes, indeed
He needs it (for another teaching)
The verse treats him as if
Mount Horeb, another name for הר סיני

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה learns from סמוכים in משנה תורה. Still, he does not forbid a בעל קרי from learning Torah, because those verses teach the reward of one who teaches his son Torah.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains how רבי יהודה can allow a בעל קרי to learn Torah without going against his own way of reading verses.

phrases.english: They said: Yes, in משנה תורה he does expound verses next to each other,
phrases.notes: משנה תורה here means the book of דברים.

phrases.english: but these side-by-side verses he needs
for the other teaching of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi.
phrases.notes: These are the same פסוקים used for the בעל קרי rule back in Step 15.

phrases.english: For Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
Whoever teaches his son Torah,
the verse treats him
as if he received it from Mount Horeb.
As it says: 'And you shall make them known to your children and your children's children,'
phrases.notes: דברים 4:9

phrases.english: and right after it is written:

phrases.aramaic: ״יוֹם אֲשֶׁר עָמַדְתָּ לִפְנֵי ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ בְּחוֹרֵב״.
phrases.english: 'The day that you stood before ה׳ your God at Horeb.'
phrases.notes: דברים 4:10

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: אִין בְּמִשְׁנֵה תוֹרָה דָּרֵישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After steps 20-21 proved that רבי יהודה uses סמוכים in משנה תורה, this step answers the question from step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The verses are needed for another teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since רבי יהודה learns from סמוכים in משנה תורה, he should forbid a בעל קרי from learning Torah.
steps.terutzMaskana: He does learn from סמוכים there, but these verses are used for רבי יהושע בן לוי's teaching about teaching one's son Torah.

steps.title: A משנה: רבי יהודה exempts severely impure people from immersion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה. A זב who saw קרי, a נדה who discharged semen, and a woman who saw blood during relations all need טבילה, but רבי יהודה exempts them.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה: A זב who had a seminal emission, a נדה who discharged semen, and a woman who saw blood during relations all need immersion. And רבי יהודה exempts them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a משנה about טבילה for קרי to build a new challenge against רבי יהודה's ruling (step 14) that a בעל קרי may say ברכות. The next step draws that challenge out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All these people are already impure in a stronger way and cannot become fully pure yet. The first opinion says they still need טבילה for the קרי. רבי יהודה says they do not need it, and the גמרא will now examine what that tells us.

keyTerms.meaning: A man impure because of an unusual discharge
A נדה who discharged semen
Immersion in a מקוה
Exempts

phrases.english: We learned in a משנה:
A זב who had a seminal emission,
and a נדה who discharged semen,
a woman who had relations and saw blood,
all need immersion.
And Rabbi Yehuda exempts them.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן זָב שֶׁרָאָה קֶרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 22 answers the סמוכים question, the גמרא opens a new line of attack on רבי יהודה's ruling in step 14, using this משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first opinion requires טבילה for these severely impure people who also have קרי. רבי יהודה exempts them.

steps.title: רבי יהודה Only Exempts a זב
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה exempts only a זב who saw קרי, because a זב can't become pure through טבילה anyway. A plain בעל קרי still needs טבילה even according to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה only exempted a זב who saw קרי, since from the start he isn't fit for טבילה. But a person who only had קרי, רבי יהודה obligates.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a challenge out of the משנה. רבי יהודה exempted only a זב, so a plain בעל קרי still needs טבילה even according to him, which seems to clash with his ruling in step 14.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A זב stays impure with his own seven-day impurity even after he immerses, so a טבילה for the קרי achieves little. That is why רבי יהודה exempts him. A plain בעל קרי becomes fully pure through טבילה, so רבי יהודה may well require it for him.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Only up to here': this limits a ruling to the case it was said about.
A man with a special bodily discharge that makes him impure for seven days.
Someone whose immersion would actually make him pure.
Alone, only. Here: a plain בעל קרי with no other impurity.

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לֹא פָּטַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda only exempted
a zav who saw a seminal emission,
since from the start he is not fit for immersion,
phrases.notes: Even after he immerses he's still impure as a זב, so the טבילה can't make him pure.

phrases.english: but one who only had a seminal emission, he obligates.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד כָּאן לֹא פָּטַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אֶלָּא בְּזָב שֶׁרָאָה קֶרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reads the משנה quoted in step 23 as limiting רבי יהודה's exemption to a זב, which implies he requires טבילה for a plain בעל קרי. This challenges his ruling in step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the ruling to a special case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה exempts every בעל קרי from טבילה.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה exempts only a זב, who can't become pure through טבילה anyway. A plain בעל קרי still needs טבילה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's ruling in our משנה (step 14) that a בעל קרי recites ברכות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי יהודה exempts only a זב from טבילה, then he requires טבילה for a plain בעל קרי. That seems to contradict his lenient view that a בעל קרי may say ברכות.

steps.title: Maybe the Argument Shows How Far the רבנן Go
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises the other possibility: maybe רבי יהודה exempts even a plain בעל קרי. In that case the משנה used the זב case only to show how far the רבנן go.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say: the same is true even for a plain בעל קרי, that רבי יהודה exempts him too. They argue about a זב who saw קרי only to show you the strength of the רבנן's view.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a way to defend רבי יהודה against the challenge in step 24. Perhaps he exempts every בעל קרי after all. The next step knocks this defense down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument is that the משנה chose the hardest case for the רבנן on purpose. Even when the טבילה seems useless, as with a זב, the רבנן still require it. On this reading, the case chosen tells us nothing about where רבי יהודה's exemption stops.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if you say': introduces a possible objection.
The same law applies.
To show you how strong or far-reaching someone's opinion is.

steps.confusionAlert: Both possibilities in steps 24 and 25 are about רבי יהודה's view. The question is only whether his exemption covers every בעל קרי or just a זב.

phrases.english: And if you say: the same is true
that even one who only had a seminal emission
Rabbi Yehuda also exempts,
and the fact that they disagree
about a zav who saw a seminal emission
is to show you how far the Rabbis go.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: הוּא הַדִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רבי יהודה against the challenge in step 24 by offering another reason the משנה might have used the זב case.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 24 that רבי יהודה exempts only a זב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה may have picked the זב case to show how strict the רבנן are, not to show where רבי יהודה's exemption ends.

steps.title: Look at the Last Case of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the objection by pointing to the סיפא: a woman who saw blood during relations needs טבילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say the end of the משנה: a woman who had relations and saw blood needs טבילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins to knock down the defense from step 25 by pointing to the last case of the same משנה. It is setting up the analysis in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The סיפא is a case where טבילה is required. The גמרא will ask whose opinion this case follows, and the answer will show what רבי יהודה holds.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Say the end': look at the last part of the משנה.
A woman having marital relations.

phrases.english: Say the last part:
a woman who had relations and saw blood
needs immersion.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts rejecting the defense of רבי יהודה in step 25 by bringing evidence from the end of the same משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה does not exempt every בעל קרי.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The סיפא of the משנה quoted in step 23.

steps.title: This Case Can't Be the רבנן's View
steps.stepSummary: If the סיפא followed the רבנן, it would be obvious through a קל וחומר from the זב case. So the משנה would not need to teach it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? If it's the רבנן, it's obvious! They obligate a זב who saw קרי, even though he wasn't fit for טבילה from the start. So a woman who saw blood during relations, who was fit for טבילה from the start, surely needs טבילה too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whose opinion the סיפא follows. It shows the case would be pointless to teach if it were the רבנן's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן require טבילה even for a זב, whose immersion seems useless. The woman was fully able to become pure when the קרי reached her. So it is obvious that the רבנן would require טבילה for her as well.

keyTerms.meaning: According to whose opinion is this taught?
Obvious; there is no need to teach it.
All the more so (a קל וחומר).

phrases.english: According to whom is it taught?
If you say the Rabbis, that's obvious!
Now, if a zav who saw a seminal emission,
who from the start is not fit for immersion,
the Rabbis obligate;
then a woman who had relations and saw blood,
who from the start was fit for immersion,
phrases.notes: She hadn't seen blood yet when her husband's semen reached her, so a טבילה would have made her pure.

phrases.english: all the more so, no?!

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמַאן קָתָנֵי לַהּ? אִילֵּימָא לְרַבָּנַן — פְּשִׁיטָא!
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks whose opinion the סיפא from step 26 follows, and rules out the רבנן.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the סיפא follows the רבנן or רבי יהודה.

steps.title: So the סיפא Must Follow רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The סיפא must follow רבי יהודה, and it was taught for a specific reason. The explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't it רבי יהודה's view? And it was taught specifically.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that the סיפא follows רבי יהודה. It is setting up the point that this case was taught on purpose, which continues next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The סיפא teaches רבי יהודה's exemption even when the קרי came before the נדה impurity. That exemption is specific to a person whose impurity lingers anyway; a plain בעל קרי still needs טבילה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Rather, isn't it…': the גמרא points to the only remaining option.
Specifically, exactly as stated; taught on purpose.

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה exempts the woman from טבילה even when the קרי came before she became נדה, because her impurity lingers anyway. A plain בעל קרי still needs טבילה.

phrases.english: Rather, isn't it Rabbi Yehuda's view,
and it was taught specifically,

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 27: the סיפא must be רבי יהודה's view.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The סיפא follows רבי יהודה and was taught on purpose.
